\section[a influência]{a influência — the influence}

\label{lesson:PT-C354-influencia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to make difficult, then the Portuguese for to favour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a influência}
\textbf{a influência} — \textquotedblleft{}the influence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A avó teve muita influência na minha vida.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My grandmother had a lot of influence on my life.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ter influência sobre} — to have influence over.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{influência} is a learned borrowing from Medieval Latin \emph{īnfluentia} (EtymDB), built on Latin \emph{īnfluere} \textquotedblleft{}to flow or run into\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a influência}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a influência}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a influência}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to make difficult, then the Portuguese for to favour, then say \emph{a influência} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a influência mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The influence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[influenciar]{influenciar — to influence}

\label{lesson:PT-C354-influenciar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to favour, then the Portuguese for the influence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: influenciar}
\textbf{influenciar} — \textquotedblleft{}to influence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os amigos influenciam muito os jovens.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Friends influence young people a lot.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Influenciar alguém} takes a direct object, with no preposition.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{influenciar} is built on \emph{influência} \textquotedblleft{}influence\textquotedblright{}, from Medieval Latin \emph{īnfluentia} (EtymDB), on Latin \emph{īnfluere} \textquotedblleft{}to flow in\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{influenciar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{influenciar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to favour, then the Portuguese for the influence, then say \emph{influenciar} again

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[agravar]{agravar — to make worse, to aggravate}

\label{lesson:PT-C354-agravar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the influence, then the Portuguese for to influence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: agravar}
\textbf{agravar} — \textquotedblleft{}to make worse, to aggravate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O frio agravou a minha tosse.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The cold made my cough worse.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Agravar-se} — to get worse.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{agravar} comes from Latin \emph{aggravāre} \textquotedblleft{}to add to the weight of, to make worse\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{gravis} \textquotedblleft{}heavy\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[atenuar]{atenuar — to ease, to soften, to lessen}

\label{lesson:PT-C354-atenuar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to influence, then the Portuguese for to make worse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: atenuar}
\textbf{atenuar} — \textquotedblleft{}to ease, to soften, to lessen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Este comprimido atenua a dor.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{This pill eases the pain.}
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \emph{aliviar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{atenuar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{attenuāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make thin or weak\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{tenuis} \textquotedblleft{}thin\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[compensar]{compensar — to make up for, to compensate; to be worth it}

\label{lesson:PT-C354-compensar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to make worse, then the Portuguese for to ease.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: compensar}
\textbf{compensar} — \textquotedblleft{}to make up for, to compensate; to be worth it\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Trabalhei no sábado para compensar o dia que perdi.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I worked on Saturday to make up for the day I lost.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Compensa!} — it is worth it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{compensar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{compēnsāre} \textquotedblleft{}to weigh several things with one another, to balance\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{pēnsāre} \textquotedblleft{}to weigh\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{pendere}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to make worse, then the Portuguese for to ease, then say \emph{compensar} again
\end{itemize}
